A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how aging results, which are usually derived for the trap model in the high-temperature limit, are in fact true in a more general situation.
we have established a connection between K-processes and the REM-like trap models, and have obtained a new aging result for the latter models.

we show that, for the REM-like model at low temperature, the process of the number of visited traps in a finite time interval is a K-process, and that this process is a good approximation to the process of the total number of visited traps.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aging in the REM-like trap models at low temperature is a consequence of the K-processes that are obtained as scaling limits.
the K-processes are a natural class of Markov chains which exhibit a variety of aging properties, including the so-called ``subaging'' property.
the K-processes provide a simple and elegant way to describe the scaling limit of the REM-like model ``at low temperatures'', and to obtain aging results for those processes.
